To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an efficient prokaryotic system for the production of the human GM-activator protein, which is functionally identical to the natural protein.
we have produced, in Escherichicoli, a functionally active recombinant GM2-activa-tor protein that was able to restore the degradation of the ganglioside substrate in a mutant fibroblast cell line.
a human GM2- activator protein was produced in E. coli, purified, and found to be functionally active.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel and efficient method for the production of human GM2- activator protein, which is an essential component of the enzyme that degrades ganglioside (GM2) in lysosomes.
the production of a functionally pure and active recombinant human GM2- activator protein.
the expression of the human GM-activator protein, a protein of 18.5 kDa, which is essential in the catabolism of the glycosphingolipid GM2 in mammalian tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GM2-AP cDNA was cloned and expressed in E. coli, and the expressed GM2-AP was purified to near homogeneity and shown to be biologically active.
this is a useful expression system for the production of a functionally and structurally intact human GM2- activator protein.
this is a very useful and powerful method for the production of GM2-activators for research purposes.

we have successfully cloned, expressed and purified a human GM2- activator in Escherichi a coli and that this protein can be used to correct the deficiency of GM2- activators in cultured cells from patients with the AB variant.
the hexahistidyl GM2-activators produced in E. coli are fully active in the degradation of GM2 in the AB variant of the GM2-ganglio-sidosis.
we have succeeded in expressing the GM2- activator protein in Eschrichia coli and have shown that the protein is functionally active.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GM2-Activator protein, a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-linked protein, is produced in E. coli and that it is functional.
the hexahistidinyl tail is not an impediment to the function of the recombinant protein.
